semantics: FLOOR (non-regression), not an exact-match ledger: --check FAILS only when the candidate vector is BELOW this baseline in some dimension; it PASSES on an exact hold or a genuine improvement. Ratchet the floor explicitly via --write — up after a real fix, or down only with deliberate, reviewed intent — never implicitly.

sources.xfail_total / xfail_by_priority: docs/xfail-census.json ('total', 'per_classification.P0'/'P1'/'P2'); trusted only once the 'xfail-census-check' fence below proves it is not stale.
sources.unit_tests_passed: with `--unit-junit <glob>` (what CI uses): sum of `tests - failures - errors - skipped` over the `unit` job's own `unit-junit-<shard>.xml` reports, from the same run — the suite is measured once, by the job that owns it. Without the flag (local runs): final summary line of `<python> -m pytest tests/ -q`, the same invocation `make test` runs, executed by this script itself. Either way a red suite — or, in JUnit mode, a missing/unreadable/empty report — aborts the whole gate before any comparison.
sources.fences_passing: each name's own script/mode, invoked exactly as its Makefile target does: check-bpmn-error-allowlist -> scripts/ci/check_bpmn_error_allowlist.py; check-start-process-fence -> scripts/ci/check_start_process_fence.py; effect-chokepoint-fence -> scripts/ci/check_effect_chokepoint_fence.py; verify-amh-contract-pin -> scripts/ci/verify_amh_contract_pin.py; xfail-census-check -> scripts/ci/generate_xfail_census.py --check
